scope.activity: Read the current candidate.2 tolerance wording and match its categories to the saved grader operations and tolerance values, including the ordinary_singleton regression.

tolerance_mapping.conclusion: All six saved operations use float32, singleton reduction groups and order -41 or +41. The public strict tolerance now names this scope explicitly.
All seven saved float32 regressions use orders outside -41/+41. ordinary_singleton uses ord=2, shape [2,1,3] and dim [1], so it now unambiguously belongs to this category.
All three saved float64 operations, including the two singleton +/-41 operations, retain the declared float64 tolerance.

resolution.wording: task.json and its authoring source now restrict the strict float32 singleton tolerance to ord=-41/+41. README and migration review describe the same task-only clarification.
resolution.interpretation: The tolerance values are the same values recorded in the candidate.1 independent review and used by the saved grader. This resolves a broader statement in the old contract; it does not assert that candidate.1 ordinary_singleton was originally scored with the stricter tolerance.
resolution.identity: The task revision advances to candidate.2 while the scoring revision remains candidate.1. Existing physical runs and their outcomes retain their original task identity and are not relabelled as candidate.2 executions.
resolution.unchanged_evidence_scope: The earlier mathematical oracle check and its coverage limits remain historical evidence. This follow-up neither reruns those calculations nor expands negative-order zero-input coverage, shape/dtype evidence, batch-level compilation diagnostics, runtime validation or admission claims.
